codes.title: Codes
codes.revoke_confirm: Revoke {code}? It will unlock nothing any more.
codes.reason_hint: Optional, kept with the code (max. 255 characters).
codes.expiry_hint: Date and time (server time). Empty = never expires. Promo and invite access follows it at once.
codes.section_facts_hint: What the code is and where it leads.
codes.section_status_hint: A revoked code unlocks nothing and cannot be claimed.
codes.section_activity_hint: Every event of this code, newest first. No emails, devices shortened.
codes.section_certificate_hint: Rebuilt from the stored signature: the same data as when it was signed.
codes.no_signature: No signature stored for this code: only the QR SVG can be made.

generate.title: Generate a code
generate.meta: One code, signed with ML-DSA-65; QR SVG and signature are archived on the server.
generate.redirect_hint: Where the reader lands after the QR landing page.
generate.template_coa: Printed on the certificate of authenticity and signed with the code.
generate.template_print: Printed on the access certificate and signed with the code.
generate.sign_failed: Signing failed, the code has no signature: {error}
generate.archive_failed: Could not archive {file} on the server.
generate.how_hint: Same steps as the old generate page.
generate.how_1: The server stores a new 8-character code.
generate.how_2: This browser signs all fields with the server key; the signature is stored with the code.
generate.how_3: Download the QR SVG, the certificate PDF and the signature file.

batches.title: Batches
batches.meta: A batch signs and registers every code of an edition, with QR SVG and certificate.
batches.complete_warning: A complete batch of this edition exists ({done} codes, {date}). Add a new edition to the server configuration to make more, or create one anyway.
batches.leave_confirm: The batch is running. Stop it and leave? It can be resumed later.
batches.promo_name_hint: Printed nowhere – it names the batch, e.g. Comic Con Wien 2026.
batches.promo_toon_hint: Scanning a code opens this toon.

users.title: Users & roles
users.section_account_hint: How the account came in and what it has.
users.section_roles_hint: Changes apply right away; the role is checked on every request.
users.revoke_own_admin: Remove your own admin role? You lose access to this app.
users.section_characters_hint: Characters this account may wear as reader avatar. Defaults (every member) come from the setting AVATAR_DEFAULT_UNLOCKS and cannot be revoked here.
users.character_looks: Extra looks with an A-pose, persona/look (comma separated, optional)
users.section_reviews_hint: Who may publish what, per toon (or every toon). Without a rule an account publishes story content directly; physical catalog changes always need "Publishes physical items". "Reviews publishing requests" and "Publishes physical items" grant something, "Submits for review" restricts.
users.rule_physical_hint: Publishes physical catalog changes (physical items, editions, products) and decides other people's requests for them. Without it, even an admin only submits.
users.section_reading_hint: How far this account has read each chapter (from its save game; last read first). Guests keep their save game in their browser only.
users.reading_none: No save game on the server yet.
users.reading_again: read to the end, reading again
users.rule_reviewer_hint: Gets a mail for every request in this toon and publishes it or sends it back (physical changes excepted).
users.rule_needs_review_hint: May not publish in this toon, only submit for review.

reading.title: Reading
reading.stops_label: Readers who have not finished the chapter yet, in 10 % steps: {stops}
reading.none: No member has opened a chapter yet.

catalog.title: Catalog
catalog.meta: Shop & codes: toons, permissions, code types and meta – stored in the database; every change is in the history and can be undone.
catalog.undo_changed_message: This entry was changed after this change. Undoing it anyway also drops the later changes (they stay in the history).
catalog.not_found: “{id}” is not in the catalog (any more).
catalog.delete_message: It is gone from the catalog at once; the history keeps it, so it can be brought back with undo.
catalog.in_use: “{id}” cannot be deleted – it is still used by:
catalog.discard_message: The open entry has changes that are not saved.
catalog.id_hint: Stable, cannot be changed later (letters, digits, _ and -).
catalog.id_invalid: Not a valid id for this kind.
catalog.confirm_save_types: Code types decide what a scanned code may do (claim, signup, permissions) – the change applies to every code of this type at once.
catalog.advanced_hint: Skills, effects, wear and other rarer fields – applied as you type once the JSON is valid.
catalog.in_creator: Items, recipes, albums, products and editions are edited in the creator – drafts, versions and review there; physical changes are published only by accounts with "Publishes physical items".

content.title: Content
content.meta: Read-only: everything in the content store. Editing happens in the creator.

settings.title: Settings
settings.meta: Runtime settings of the API. They apply to the next request, no deploy needed.
settings.section_limits_hint: Per client IP and hour. Every attempt counts. 0 = no limit.
settings.scan_limit_per_hour_hint: Scans per hour from one network (the QR landing page). Events share one IP (one Wi-Fi) – keep this high. 0 = no limit.
settings.lookup_limit_per_hour_hint: Codes checked per hour from one IP in the viewer or via the API (/code/, /access/). Low against guessing codes. 0 = no limit.
settings.newsletter_per_hour_hint: At most this many mails per hour through the SMTP account while a newsletter sends – every mail of the last hour counts, sign-in codes too. Ask your mail host for its limit. 0 = no limit.
settings.newsletter_batch_hint: How many mails one batch sends – the cron every 5 minutes, or one step of "Send now". 20 per 5 minutes reaches 200 an hour. At most 25: a batch stops after 25 seconds, one mail per second.

emails.title: Emails
emails.meta_templates: Every email the API sends, rendered with sample values.
emails.transport_log: Transport log: mails are written to the server's logs/mail.log, nothing is delivered.
emails.subject: Subject
emails.recipients_hint: Who gets the admin notifications (e.g. a new ownership claim). One address per line, at most {max}.

help.lists: Search, filters, sort and page live in the URL: share or bookmark a view. The pager and the filters sit in the bottom bar (under “More” on narrow screens). Ctrl+K or / opens the command palette.
help.codes: Search matches part of a code. Select rows for a bulk revoke, unrevoke or expiry change; the CSV export takes the current filter. A click on a row opens the code beside the list.
help.batches: Per code a batch runs sign → database → QR SVG → certificate PDF → signature. The manifest is saved on the server after every code, so a batch can be paused, aborted and resumed. The history has the ZIP and the print sheet of every batch.
help.users: Search matches part of an email; filter by role and newsletter opt-in. A user's page shows owned codes, sessions, roles and reader characters.
help.events: Every scan, unlock and claim, newest first. Filter by event type, code, edition, toon and date.
help.content: Per toon every file of the content store with its newest and its published version. Editing and publishing happen in the creator (“In the creator”).
help.settings: Changes apply to the next request, no deploy needed. “Use default” goes back to the default value.
help.homepage: Which editions the scutoons.com homepage shows, in this order (each with sizes, variants, price, "Buy" and its images as a slider). The variant decides the images. Live once saved (browser cache up to 1 minute).
help.emails: The API is the only sender of email. “Sent mails” lists every mail it tried to send, newest first: template, address, language, sent or failed (with the error). It never shows the content – a sign-in mail carries a one-time code. Entries are kept 180 days. “Templates” shows every email in German and English with sample values, and who gets the admin notifications. Texts live in the server's templates/mail/texts.php; a new email is added there (agents/PLATFORM.md “Emails”).
help.assets: Every media file on the CDN storage, grouped into assets: the files of one medium in several sizes or formats (480p / 720p / 1080p, WebP next to PNG, 1x / 3x) are one asset. Content keeps referencing the files by their CDN paths – nothing here changes what readers load unless you replace, rename or relink. Delete works only when nothing uses the asset. "Rescan" registers new files on the storage and rebuilds the list of uses.
help.catalog: One tab per kind. Click an entry to edit it next to the list; “New …” adds one. ↑ / ↓ change the order (the order the apps show). Saving checks the entry against the rest of the catalog: what is wrong is listed above the form. An entry that something still uses (e.g. a permission by a code type) cannot be deleted – the uses are listed.
help.catalog_history: Every change (also order changes and the Homepage list) is in the history: per entry under its form, per kind behind “History”. “Undo” brings back the state before that change and is itself a change. If the entry was changed again since, it asks first (“Undo anyway”).
help.catalog_kinds: Main toons are created here only (id, name, redirect URL); the creator then fills content and meta (“Fill it in the creator”). Code types decide what a scanned code may do – saving one asks first. The products on the landing page are chosen on the Homepage page.
help.calendar: The public events list (scutoons.com/events): upcoming dates first, past ones below – the page sorts by date itself. Saving stores a new version of the events document in the content store and publishes it; live within a minute (cache). Older versions stay in its history.
help.reading: Per chapter: how many members started it and read it to the end. "Reading" are those who have not finished it yet; "Where they are" shows where they stand (10 bars = 0–100 %). Members only – guests keep their save game in their browser. One account’s reading is on its page.

homepage.title: Homepage
homepage.meta: The limited editions on the homepage: product, variant, order.
homepage.section_featured_hint: Top to bottom as on the page. At most {max}.

claims.title: Claims
claims.legacy_registration: registered by the old email form, no account
claims.section_statement_hint: In the claimant's words, as sent.
claims.section_files_hint: Photos or PDFs the claimant attached (receipt, the item with its certificate). Click to open full size.
claims.section_certificate_hint: The server's check of the code's certificate: signature against the published key and our records.
claims.section_decision_hint: A note is required either way. The buttons are in the bottom bar.
claims.transfer_explain: Moves the code and its items to {email}. Both the previous owner and the claimant get an email.
claims.transfer_note_hint: Why the claimant is right (kept in the ownership history).
claims.reject_explain: The code stays where it is. The claimant gets an email that the claim was rejected.
claims.reject_note_hint: Internal only: the claimant does not see this note.
claims.choose_item_hint: This code was never registered and can be several items: choose the one the claimant has.
claims.choose_item_needed: Choose which item the code is for, then try again.
claims.confirm_transfer: This moves {code} and its items to {email}. Both owners get an email. Only another transfer can undo it.
claims.confirm_reject: {code} stays with its owner. {email} gets an email that the claim was rejected.
claims.section_history_hint: Every ownership change of this code, newest first.
claims.code_history_hint: Shows accounts: this is the support record. Elsewhere this page does not show who owns the code.
claims.section_transfer_code_hint: For support cases outside a claim, e.g. a sale both people told us about.
claims.transfer_to_hint: The new owner's email or account id. The account must exist.
claims.confirm_transfer_code: This moves {code} and its items to {to}. The previous and the new owner get an email.
claims.help_list: Readers who say a registered code is theirs file a claim with a statement and evidence. Search matches part of a code or the claimant's email; filter by status, code or account. A click on a row opens the claim.
claims.help_status_transferred: Decided for the claimant: the code moved to their account.
claims.help_status_rejected: Decided against the claimant: the code stayed.
claims.help_detail: Everything needed to decide one claim: the statement, the evidence, the certificate check, who owned the code when the claim was filed and who owns it now, and the code's ownership history.
claims.help_decide_1: Read the statement and open the evidence.
claims.help_decide_2: Compare with the certificate check, the ownership history and other claims on the code.
claims.help_decide_3: Write a note and transfer or reject (bottom bar). Both ask once more.
claims.help_transfer: Moves the code and its items to the claimant and mails both owners. The note goes into the ownership history.
claims.help_reject: Leaves the code where it is and mails the claimant. The note stays internal.
claims.help_transfer_code: Moves the code and its items to another account outside a claim; a note is required, both owners get an email.

assets.title: Assets
assets.standard_hint: Files off the media standard (images WebP; video MP4 / WebM). Converting writes a NEW file beside the old one – a CDN path is never overwritten – and then points every use to it (content as a new draft, the catalog directly). The old file stays until “Unused” cleans it up.
assets.standard_totals: {files} files off the standard ({size}): {convert} to convert, {twin} already have their WebP (relink only), {rest} not fixable here
assets.fix_video: needs ffmpeg – not on the host yet
assets.standard_confirm_message: Each file gets a new WebP beside it (nothing on the CDN is overwritten); then every use points to the new file – content as new drafts (publish them in the creator), the catalog right away. The old files stay until “Unused” cleans them up.
assets.standard_report_uses: {uses} uses: {drafts} documents as new drafts, {catalog} catalog entries updated, {manual} by hand
assets.standard_report_relink_failed: The new files are uploaded, but relinking failed: {error}
assets.standard_report_drafts: New drafts – check and publish them in the creator:
assets.empty: No assets – run "Rescan" to register the files of the storage.
assets.rescan_hint: Register new files of the storage and rebuild the uses (reads the storage, never writes)
assets.scanned: {files} files read, {created} new assets; {usages} uses, {missing} pointing to missing files.
assets.missing_hint: Content or the catalog references these paths, but no such file is on the storage.
assets.unused_hint: Files nothing references – published content, drafts, the catalog or app code. The list is checked against the content right now, and again when you delete. Older app builds and old content versions may still point to them.
assets.cleanup_message: {size} are removed from the CDN for good (no undo). Nothing that is referenced right now is deleted.
assets.settings_hint: The public CDN and the vault (BUNNY_PROTECTED_* / PROTECTED_*: scores' files, release audio). From the server configuration (locally: the repository-root .env). Passwords and keys are never shown.
assets.bandwidth_value: Last {days} days: {size} served, {requests} requests, cache hit rate {hit} %.
assets.bandwidth_load_hint: Asks bunny.net for the pull zone statistics of the last 30 days.
assets.bandwidth_no_key: Needs the bunny.net account API key (BUNNY_API_KEY).
assets.shape_mask: One colour – the page colours it (mask)
assets.shape_asis: Several colours – shown as it is
assets.replace_hint: New bytes at the same path: nothing in the content changes, the CDN cache is purged, the old file is kept as the previous version. Other files made from it (480p …) are marked stale – regenerate them below.
assets.rename_hint: Copies the files to the new name and points every use at them (content as new drafts). The old files stay until nothing uses them.
assets.publish_too: Publish changed content right away (only where the newest version was published)
assets.renamed: {files} files copied, {uses} uses relinked in {drafts} documents.
assets.relink_hint: Points every use of one file at another existing file (e.g. the trailer at the prologue’s 720p). Content gets new drafts; catalog files are changed on this server only.
assets.relinked: {uses} uses changed in {docs} documents; {manual} catalog files need a manual change.
assets.optimize_hint: Queues a job; it runs on a machine with ffmpeg: php bin/console assets:jobs. Videos: 480p / 720p / 1080p H.264 (fast start); images: WebP.
assets.job_queued: Job #{id} queued – run php bin/console assets:jobs.
assets.delete_hint: Removes every file of the asset (all versions) from the storage. Refused while published content or the catalog uses it.
assets.delete_ok: Nothing uses it – {files} files can go.
assets.delete_force: Delete anyway – only drafts use it (they would show a missing file)
assets.delete_refused: Refused: the asset is in use.
assets.term_asset_text: One medium (the trailer loop, a cover, a song) with all its files.
assets.term_version_text: Each replacement of a file in place makes a new version; the old bytes are kept until deleted.
assets.term_rendition_text: One file of a version: the original, a quality level (480p = low, 720p = medium, 1080p = high), a width, a WebP copy, a poster.
assets.term_usage_text: Where content (published or the working draft) or the catalog references a file.
assets.tile_set_hint: A map tile set: the tiles of one layer version (agents/MAP.md). Nothing uses this version – it goes as a whole.

calendar.title: Events
calendar.meta: Dates on scutoons.com/events: concerts, readings, streams.
calendar.draft_newer: The newest version ({at}) is not published yet
calendar.invalid: Every event needs a date, a title and a city.
calendar.conflict: Someone saved the events meanwhile – reloaded, please redo your change.

changes.title: Proposed changes
changes.note: Nothing is changed until you apply.
changes.undo_catalog: Undo: History on the catalog page
changes.calendar_draft: Saved as a draft – publish it on the Calendar page
changes.changed_since: Changed since the AI read it – ask again.
changes.dismiss_message: Nothing is changed. It stays in the list under Dismissed.

server_errors.title: Server errors
server_errors.no_log: There is no log yet – nothing has been logged.
server_errors.truncated: The log has {size}; only its last 512 KB are read.
server_errors.help: The newest entries of the PHP error logs – the API's and the QR app's – newest first, with the lines that follow an entry (a stack trace) under "Details". Messages only: e-mail addresses, tokens and passwords are masked, the server's folder is cut from file paths. Only the last 512 KB of a log are read.

newsletter.title: Newsletters
newsletter.meta: Mass mails to members and contacts, sent in small batches through the SMTP account.
newsletter.new_title_hint: Only you see it, e.g. "Chapter 3 release".
newsletter.state_line: {queued} waiting · {sent} of {limit} mails in the last hour
newsletter.state_no_cron: No cron set up: mails only go out while this page sends ("Send now").
newsletter.state_cron: The host's cron sends a batch every few minutes.
newsletter.state_log: Transport log: mails are written to the server's logs/mail.log, nothing is delivered.
newsletter.batch_limit: Hourly limit reached – the rest goes out later.
newsletter.audiences_hint: Each address once. Unsubscribed and bounced addresses never, our own (@scutoons.com) only when ticked.
newsletter.subject: Subject
newsletter.picture_webp: WebP picture: Outlook on desktop doesn't show it. A JPG or PNG works in every mail program.
newsletter.variable_name: the name (empty when there is none)
newsletter.variable_signin: Sign-in button (personal: members “Sign in”, QR owners “Create your account”)
newsletter.body_hint: A blank line starts a paragraph. A line [Button text](https://…) becomes a button, a line ![description](picture) a picture, a line {signin_line} the personal sign-in button (one click signs in, valid 14 days; the preview shows a member's). {example} = the name, or the word after | when there is none.
newsletter.start_message: From now on the batches send it ({limit} mails per hour at most). You can pause any time.
newsletter.delete_message: Only the newsletter goes; the sent-mail log keeps its rows.
newsletter.missing_locale: {count} contacts have no language yet – set it on the Contacts page.
newsletter.missing_text: Subject and text in {locale} are missing – some recipients read {locale}.
newsletter.locked_sending: Sending – pause to fix a typo in subject or text.
newsletter.locked_done: Sent. Nothing can change any more.
newsletter.contacts_meta: Addresses that are no account: the old QR form and your event lists.
newsletter.import_text_hint: One per line. Optional: a name and de / en, separated by comma, semicolon or tab – "ana@example.com, Ana, de".
newsletter.import_source_hint: Where these people signed up, e.g. "event:Leipzig 2026-09".
newsletter.blocked_meta: Addresses no newsletter goes to: unsubscribed, bounced or blocked by hand. Sign-in mails still go.
newsletter.unblock_message: Only when the person asked for it again.

proposals.title: Proposals
proposals.not_found: This proposal does not exist (any more).

segments.title: Segments
segments.hint: Named groups of accounts, e.g. to let them invite in a campaign. Tick accounts on the list to add them, or add all that the filters find.
segments.name: Name
segments.delete_message: Its {count} accounts stay – only the group goes.
segments.add_matching_message: Every account the search and filters find, on every page.
segments.error_in_use: A campaign lets this segment invite – change the campaign first.
segments.error_name_taken: There is a segment with this name already.

campaigns.title: Campaigns
campaigns.meta: Members invite people without an account with a gift
campaigns.name: Name
campaigns.name_hint: Only admins see it, e.g. “Advent invites”
campaigns.stop_message: No new invites. The invites already sent keep waiting until their own end.
campaigns.ends_at_hint: Invites can be accepted until then.
campaigns.gift_own_hint: Members pick something from their inventory, as with any gift.
campaigns.gift_campaign: A campaign item, given by SCUTOONS
campaigns.gift_campaign_hint: Every invite carries this item; the member’s inventory stays as it is.
campaigns.gift_locked: Invites are out – the gift stays as it is.
campaigns.stock_hint: Empty = no limit. Invites stop when they are gone.
campaigns.payer_scutoons_hint: The friend enters a shipping address when joining; it appears under Invites → To ship.
campaigns.payer_member_hint: The gift waits: hello@ gets a mail, an admin sends the member a payment link or the bank details and marks it paid.
campaigns.countries_hint: Country codes, e.g. AT, DE, CH
campaigns.access_keep_hint: Whoever joins during the campaign keeps reading – also after the invite code ends.
campaigns.access_until_hint: Then they need a product. Their account and items stay.
campaigns.per_day_hint: Per member, together with the 10 gifts a day.
campaigns.inviters_all_hint: Every account – also members who join later.
campaigns.tick_matching_message: Every account the search and filters find, on every page.
campaigns.payment_hint: Send each member a payment link or the bank details by hand. When the money is there, press “Payment received” – then the invite goes out.
campaigns.to_ship_hint: Joined friends with a physical gift and an address. Press “Shipped” when it has left.
campaigns.paid_message: {member} paid – the invite goes to {friend} now.
campaigns.error_window: The campaign must end after it starts.
campaigns.error_item: A campaign gift needs an item from the catalog.
campaigns.error_payer: A physical gift: choose who pays.
campaigns.error_price: Enter the price for the member.
campaigns.error_countries: A physical gift: enter the countries it ships to.
campaigns.error_access: Choose when the invitees’ reading ends.
campaigns.error_locked: Invites are out – the gift stays as it is.
campaigns.error_has_invites: Invites were sent – stop the campaign instead.
campaigns.error_segment_mode: A segment invites here – change who is in it in Users & roles.

push.title: Push notifications
push.meta: Readers who switched on “Tell me when a new chapter is out” on their account page. Nothing is sent automatically.
push.off: Push is off on this server: no VAPID keys (VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY / VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY).
push.send_message: Every subscribed browser gets the notification now. It can't be taken back.
push.send_again: This chapter was announced {count} time(s) before.
push.test_none: None of your browsers is subscribed – switch on notifications on your account page in the reader first.
push.team_hint: They go by themselves (proposals, publishing requests, open drafts, the Embassy reminder) – each person switches them on in their tool under Notifications. Browsers: Creator {creator} · Admin {admin} · Embassy {embassy}. A test goes only to your own browsers in that tool.
